title: This Giant Clam Never Hunts. It Farms Its Own Food
subject: giant clam

scenes.text: This clam is as big as a bathtub, and it never hunts.
The giant clam grows to about four feet long and close to 500 pounds.
It can't chase food. So it farms it.
Tiny algae live inside its flesh. By day, the clam opens wide so they get sunlight.
In return, the algae supply roughly two thirds of the clam's food.
Its edge is dotted with tiny eyespots that spot shadows. A farmer and a guard, for around a century.

description:
This clam is as big as a bathtub, and it never hunts.
The giant clam can reach about four feet long and close to 500 pounds. It farms tiny algae inside its tissue, which supply roughly 65 to 70 percent of its food, and it lives for around a century.
Would you rather farm like a clam or hunt like a shark?
first_comment: The old story that giant clams trap divers is a myth: they close too slowly to trap a person. What's the biggest sea creature you've seen in person?
